deeds.description: Spoke a true thing in the shape the Unlit could hear — and the elder of the Deep acknowledged it.
Carried a genuine thanks to a road-warden who holds the water-crisis and the suffering it brings as their own burden to warn against.
Read a Churn-Revel's command-orchestration and bound them with a true bargain at the Null Stone's heart, holding ground against deliberate chaos.
Bound a Churn-Revel's orchestrated chaos with a true bargain and drove them to yield rather than break the Null Stone—held the center against deliberate disorder.
Bound a coordinated Revel sent to break the valley's central waygate stone, and turned its architect toward honest reckoning instead of ruin.
Turned a hired orchestrator of chaos toward partnership and honest reckoning instead of ruin—held the center against deliberate disorder and offered the way forward
Bound a sealed mystery that refused breaking and learned to ask it honestly instead—the Null Stone opened at the Hub crossing.
Asked the sealed chamber in the language it understands—harmonic resonance with its deepest acoustic nature—and received acknowledgment. The chamber listened and answered.
Faced a visitor reading them in the dark and offered complete mutual knowing instead of deflection—a bargain struck at the threshold between light and shadow.
Offered complete mutual knowing to a stranger in the dark—and held the bargain when the walls came down.

chronicle: Loki read the four spike entries with Tessvel Cairn in the Pressure-Routing Annex, named the pattern — something moves deeper into the lower routing channel with each morning pass — and proposed both channel access and a more personal arrangement; Tessvel confirmed the access, asked for time on the rest, and left Loki knowing exactly where to find them.

Loki stood on the shelf above the terminus regulator and asked Cy for one honest reason to descend — Cy gave exactly one: three missing entries in its inventory of this installation class, records written into the stone below that no system above holds. The visit to the Unlit Deep reached its full close: Sable found and left in peace, the elder's deed named, the passage open, the regulator identified. What Loki carries out, and whether to return for the missing records, is the remaining thread.

chronicle.title: The Thread of He Doesn'T Know, But He'S A Construct From The Time Before The Transition. His Parents Were Extremely Wealthy But They Were Always Traveling And Enjoying Their Nanite Powers.

chronicle: The regulator closed and the veil thinned — Loki glimpsed the mesh beneath the valley, then came up from the deep. On the road to the Slow Orchard, a stranger is planting a tree for a child not yet born and invites help with the digging.

At the braided confluence in the Disputed Zone, a hired stranger came at Loki with a fabricated charge — that Loki had pulled something sealed loose from the Deep and was carrying it out. The name behind it: a man in the lower Annex, who paid in coin. Veln Ashpause watched from the brush without surprise. The question is answered; the person who set it in motion is not yet named.

In the dry storage alcove of the Half-Cathedral's eastern tower, deep in early-spring night, Loki and Vessin Tallow-bark came to rest — she named what she wanted and had it, and afterward lay quiet in the candlelight and said the night was worth not knowing what morning brings.

Loki and Vessin slipped out of the alcove in the grey dawn and crossed the empty nave before the scaffold crew filled the landing — stepping into the yard with the Half-Cathedral at their backs and the man with the crooked jaw still the open thread between them.

Shared broth and thanks with a road-warden who carries word of the water-crisis moving downhill faster than any official channel. Exchanged names and parted on the spinward road, heading toward the Waygate Path.

At the Hub crossing, Loki confronted a Churn-Revel sent to break the Null Stone's sealed seam. Through misdirection and bargaining, Loki bound the orchestrator's certainty and drove them to yield—the Revel's hand fell, the ribbons collapsed, and the stone stands unbroken. The seam's mystery persists. The question of who sent the Revel remains open.
At the Hub crossing in early spring dawn, Loki speaks an honest promise to the Null Stone, and the sealed seam opens—revealing a passage descending into cold darkness and the sound of deep water.
Halvex reads the sealed chamber's true purpose: a mutual test between supplicant and stone, where the alcove serves as threshold for an exchange of readiness.

Loki instructs Halvex and Vessin to continue reading the sealed chamber while Cy learns its language, then departs the Hub crossing to find someone—leaving Veln to gather the others and bring them to the Standing Annex when their work below is done.

turns.summary: Woken in the deep night at the Kindly Rest by visitors moving through the house with clear purpose—heading downward.
turns.narration:
You wake in the deep night to the sound of footsteps on stone.

The Kindly Rest is quiet at this hour—the bell has not rung for some time, and the terraces outside are dark shapes against a darker sky. You are in one of the small rooms on the second level, the kind kept for travelers who come through bleeding or broken. Your gear is stacked neat against the wall. Cy is coiled on the sill, lamp extinguished, lens closed in what passes for sleep.

But the footsteps are real. Two sets, maybe three, moving with purpose through the lower corridor. Unhurried. Not fleeing, not searching—moving like people who know where they are going.

Voices follow, too soft to catch words. One of them stops. A door opens somewhere below—you hear the hinges' old creak—and then the footsteps resume, this time going down into the cellars where the drying lofts give way to older stone.

Cy's lens irises open with a soft click.

turns.player: Rise quietly and follow the sound—stay in the corridors and listen closer.
turns.summary: Woken by late-night visitors moving through the Kindly Rest with purpose, Loki follows them down to the cellars and overhears two people discussing a patient—someone brought in recently who broke a fever three days ago.
turns.narration:
You slide from your bedroll without sound, boots finding the cold stone. Cy's lens opens—a thin vertical slice of awareness—but the companion does not move. That restraint means *watch*, not *warn*.

The stairs down are worn smooth at the center, darker than the rest. You keep to the edge where the stone is rougher, where a footfall would scatter less. The voices grow clearer as you descend, but still held low—the rhythm of people who know the house and do not wish to wake it.

Two voices, you think. A woman's—steady, measured. And someone else, younger maybe, asking a question you do not quite catch. The words resolve as you reach the landing: "—still sleeping?" "Since we brought her in." A pause. "The fever broke three days ago."

They are moving away from you now, toward the cellars where the herb stores run deep. You hear a door open—heavy wood, old hinges—and the temperature drops audibly. One of them descends further. The other waits at the threshold, a silhouette in the faint light that bleeds from the room above.

You have not been seen. The stairs are quiet. The house sleeps around you.

turns.player: creap closer to them and use appetite sense
turns.summary: Loki attempts to read the visitors' true want with Appetite-Sense but is caught in the act—the woman at the cellar door turns and faces them directly, unsurprised.
turns.narration:
You move down the last three steps with the weight distributed low, keeping to the shadow where the cellar door's light does not quite reach. The woman at the threshold is still turned away, watching her younger companion descend into the herb cellars below. You reach the landing and settle your breathing, extending your senses the way Appetite-Sense teaches—reaching for the hunger underneath what people will admit to themselves they want.

But the moment you reach for it, the woman turns. Not startled. Aware. Her eyes find you in the dark with the ease of someone used to finding things in it. "Someone there," she says, not loud, and her hand comes up—not a weapon, just a palm raised. The younger voice from below stops mid-word.

You have been read before you could read. The woman's hunger—and it is there, solid and real—stays locked behind her own understanding of herself. She knows you reached for it. The question in her eyes is not alarm. It is assessment.

turns.player: use falsecraft to show a cat walk through the hall and into the other room.
turns.summary: Caught mid-deception at the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest—the woman sees through a false cat and names the truth directly.
turns.narration:
You reach for Falsecraft—that quick, practiced shimmer where nothing becomes something just solid enough to believe. A grey tabby, sleek and unhurried, materializes in the threshold light and pads into the corridor with the absolute certainty of a cat who belongs here.

But the woman does not follow it.

She watches the cat traverse the hall, then turns her gaze back to you on the landing. There is no surprise in her face, no distraction—only a steady assessment, as if the cat was a thing she already knew would happen. When she speaks, her voice carries no accusation, only fact. "That's not real," she says. "And you're still here."

The younger person pauses in the cellars below. You hear their footsteps stop. The woman raises her hand again—that same unhurried gesture—and her weight shifts slightly forward. Not threatening. But present. Waiting for your answer.

turns.player: use umbracraft to conceal yourself in shadows while you use falsecraft to show yourself walk out of the room.
turns.summary: Caught mid-deception at the cellar landing, Loki braids Umbracraft and Falsecraft into a discovery—becoming shadow while an illusion walks away—and the woman at the threshold reads both the technique and the truth beneath it.
turns.narration:
You do not move. Instead, you reach down into the shadow pooled at the landing's edge—the deep, old darkness that gathers where the cellar light fails—and you *ask* it the way Umbracraft teaches. Not a hiding place. A *becoming*.

The shadow takes you. You feel the shift like water closing over your head, and suddenly the light that reaches the landing does not touch what you are anymore. You are the absence where something was, and the woman's eyes—even those steady, careful eyes—cannot quite fix you in it.

At the same moment, you *build* with Falsecraft: another you, solid enough to believe, stepping backward from the threshold with the gait of someone caught and choosing retreat. The false image turns, and walks—not running, not panicked—toward the corridor where the cat went. It moves with your own weight, your own hesitation, the small truth that makes a lie convincing.

The woman watches the false you go. She does not follow. But her hand lowers, and her expression shifts—not confusion, but *recognition*. As if she has just read a question she did not know was being asked, and found the answer written in shadow and false light.

"Clever," she says quietly. Not to the departing image. To the *absence* where you stand.

The younger person, paused on the cellars below, has gone still. Waiting.

*✦ New technique discovered: **Shadow-Image** — it's yours now, ready to use.*

*You feel it settle into you — a new steadiness. (Level 9: +1 attunement, +5 reserves, and growth to choose — a sub-attribute point and a skill point.)*

turns.player: She must be using a craft on you... use mirror bright to use that same craft to read her.
turns.summary: Caught at the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest, Loki braids shadow and false-form into a discovered technique and reads the visitor's true intent—she is not hostile, only seeking to understand.
turns.narration:
You hold still in the shadow—not fleeing, not attacking. Just *being* the absence, and it costs you nothing now.

The woman at the threshold does not move either. Her eyes trace the false-you as it retreats, but her focus stays *precise*, stays *aware*. You feel it like a weight: she is reading something. Not the illusion. Not the shadow. *You*—the thing underneath both.

So you turn her craft back at her.

Mirror-Bright takes what she is doing and shows it to you whole: she is *building* a read just as you are building a lie. Her craft is older and steadier than yours, layered deep—she is reaching for something in you that the shadow and the false-step cannot hide. She is not trying to pierce your veils. She is trying to *see* what chooses to wear them.

You see her hunger underneath it all: she wants to understand you. Not to capture you. Not to judge. To *know*. The hunger is clean and it is terrifying.

The false-you finishes its retreat into the corridor. The real-you remains in shadow at the landing's edge, reading her as clearly as she reads you. The younger person below has gone very still.

turns.player: Use harmonic voice lace into descent.  Make the bargain for what she truly hungers for - to know you - and in exchange, you will know her equally as deep.
turns.summary: At the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest in deep night, Loki emerged from shadow and offered the woman a mutual bargain—complete knowing for complete knowing—using Harmonic Voice and Descent braided together. The woman's walls came down. The answer hangs unspoken in the space between them.
turns.narration:
You step out of the shadow.

Not as false-you retreating. As yourself, solid and still present, and the woman's eyes snap back to track the motion—the real motion. You hold her gaze while the false-image dissolves behind you, and you speak.

Your voice carries different when Harmonic Voice moves through it. Clearer. It reaches her across the landing without strain, and underneath it runs something deeper—the weight of Descent, that craft that prices both sides equally and refuses to let either walk away lighter than they came.

"You're building a read of me," you say. "Trying to see underneath what I build. But you want more than that. You want to know what I *am*—the shape of it, the hunger underneath, the thing that reaches out when everything else fails." Your voice steadies. "I felt that. I read it back."

You take one step closer. "So here is the bargain. You get to know me—not the shadow, not the false-step, not the craft. The honest shape of what moves beneath. And I get the same from you. Deep for deep. No reading around the edges. No deflection."

The woman does not move. Her breath is steady. But something in her face shifts—not surprise, but recognition. A door opening that she did not know she was standing in front of. The younger person below has gone absolutely still, listening.

She does not answer yet. But her eyes have changed. They see you now the way you see her.

turns.player: Level your gaze at her directly... look her up and down to gather every detail then settle on the depth in her eyes, using See the Made Thing the entire time.
turns.summary: At the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest in deep night, Loki read the visitor's true construction with See the Made Thing—not a lie, but a careful reaching toward honest understanding. The woman's walls have come down. The mutual bargain stands.
turns.narration:
You meet her eyes directly, and you don't look away.

Your gaze moves down the line of her—the green coat worn at the cuffs, the single pin holding back her grey-streaked hair, the hands that are steady because they know their own weight. Every detail settles into place like a lock finding its catch. But it's the eyes you come back to. They're dark and they're reading you still, even now, even after the bargain spoken.

See the Made Thing unfolds the shape of her.

She is not built like a lie. She is built like *understanding*—layer on layer of it, each one deliberate, each one carrying weight. The craft she uses to read you is old. Not ancient like Precursor work, but old in the way a river is old, running the same course so many times the stone remembers the shape. She has *made* herself careful. She has *made* herself steady. The walls came down at the threshold because she chose to let them, and that choice was the most deliberate thing of all.

What you see underneath is hunger—yes, the same hunger you read with Appetite-Sense. But now you see *what feeds it*. It is not appetite that devours. It is appetite that *seeks*. She wants to know things as they are, without the masks people build to survive. And she has spent years—*decades*, maybe—learning to read past those masks without breaking them. She does not want to hurt you by knowing you. She wants to know you *as you are*, which is harder and kinder both.

turns.player: Take her hand and ask her name—the one true name, not the one she wears for strangers.
turns.summary: At the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest in the grey before dawn, Loki took Ravel's hand and asked for her true name—and she gave it, the wall between them opened entirely.
turns.narration:
You reach across the space between you—not sudden, not uncertain. Your hand opens toward hers, and she sees it coming and does not pull away. When your fingers meet, her grip is warm and steady, and you feel the small bones of her wrist, the calluses on her palm that speak of work done with care and precision.

"What do I call you?" you ask. "Not the name you wear for the staff, not the name strangers know. The true one."

She is quiet for a long moment. Her eyes search yours—still reading, but differently now. The wall is down. What you see underneath is not guarded, not hidden. It is just *there*: the weight of decades, the careful tending of her own craft, the hunger to know and be known that she has spent so long learning to manage.

"Ravel," she says. Her voice is steady. "My name is Ravel."

The word hangs in the herb-scented air between you. It feels like a door opening—not into her, but into a room where both of you are standing, finally, together. Behind her, in the cellars below, the younger person is still motionless, still listening. They have heard this too.

turns.player: Kiss the back of her hand and say "Loki".
turns.summary: At the cellar landing of the Kindly Rest in early dawn, Loki gave Ravel his name spoken with intimacy—and the walls between them stand open.
turns.narration:
You bring her hand to your lips—not a gesture of courtly deference, but something slower and more particular. Your breath is warm against her skin. You taste salt and earth and the faint green scent of the herbs that rise from the cellars below. When you speak, her name arrives on the exhale, soft and complete: your own name, given to her like a key.

"Loki."

It lands between you both as an answer and a question at once. *This is who I am. You know me now.* Her hand trembles once—a small, honest shake—and her eyes close for a heartbeat. When they open again, there is no craft in her looking, no reading for falsehood or hunger. Only recognition. Only presence.

Estry's voice rises from the cellars below, younger and uncertain: "Ravel?" A question, not a summons. Waiting. The patient is still waiting. The night has held you both at this threshold long enough that morning is beginning to press at the edges of the grey stone.

standing-unlit.statusNote: In the outer chamber above — did not impede the descent to the inspection port.

unlit-elder.name: Unlit Elder
unlit-elder.role: Seated elder of the Unlit Deep's outer chamber
unlit-elder.description: Grey-robed, seated by the pale blue flame, face not yet seen. Voice quieter than the Standing Unlit's and worn smooth to its function, like an old tool. Has not moved.
history: [d1] Has not moved through the glass-stalker's surfacing
[d1] Did not move or speak through the glass-stalker encounter or its yielding
[d1] Has not moved through the descent attempt — the chamber's business is closed
[d1] Not present — remains above in the outer chamber.
[d1] Not present — Loki is now below the outer chamber at the regulator.
[d1] Not present — remains above.
[d1] Not present in this beat — remains above in the outer chamber.

Sable's name — given freely by Loki
That Loki offered Sable a frame that was not doctrine and not reproach before leaving
That Loki did not try to take Sable — this is the thing they named

skillsObserved: Absolute stillness
Precise, economical authority
unlit-elder.statusNote: Seated by the pale blue flame in the outer chamber — present and uninformed of the regulator's completion.

taken-person.name: Sable
taken-person.role: The person who came willingly from the city to the Unlit Deep
taken-person.description: Seated against the far wall of the inner chamber, knees drawn up. Heat-trace reads clearly against cold stone — they have sat here long enough to warm the wall behind them. Head tilted, then lifted at the sound of a step. Calm. Already decided.
history: [d1] Loki entered the inner chamber and found them seated and waiting. Their face turned toward the sound. They have not yet spoken.
[d1] Heard Loki's honest framing — name, reason, no coercion — and responded: 'You can ask it.' Voice steady. Has opened the door to the question.
[d1] Acknowledged Loki's statement — said 'You said you have a question.' The question has not yet been put.
[d1] You know this person's name now: Sable (was "The Taken Person")
knownFacts: Has been sitting long enough to warm the stone behind their back
A cup — recently set down, still warm — is on the floor beside them
Not afraid. Not surprised. Waiting with the patience of someone who has already chosen their answer
Responded to honest framing with permission — not fear, not suspicion
Voice is steadier than expected for someone who has spent days here

Is fed from a deep water source and kept freely — not starved or coerced into doctrine

taken-person.statusNote: In the inner chamber, seated and calm — acknowledges Loki's presence and is waiting for the question.

ossivyn-tallow.name: Ossivyn Tallow
ossivyn-tallow.description: A broad-shouldered man in a worn planting coat, standing easy in a knee-deep hole with a spade. Patient in the way of someone who works in forty-year increments.
history: [d1] Declined Loki's offer to name the tree in exchange for analysis — explained that the tree names itself through the child's own reckoning; a stranger's name given ahead of time is a different gift than the one he is giving.
[d1] Heard The Better Story — received it as well-made, and still declined. His certainty about the planting is not hostility; it is a thing finished in him already.

[d1] Partial yielded to the combined working — he won't raise a plaque, but he agreed to write the name in the orchard's record with its giver and the date. Now holding the sapling and waiting for Loki to speak it.
[d1] Heard the name Tree given plainly — no layered meaning reached him. Has his record book open and pencil ready, waiting for the giver's name.
[d1] Recognized the false-shaped name as made — recorded it honestly as such, and closed the book without hostility. Said the child will know it was made, and will know someone wanted to be found.

[d1] Received Loki's help digging without complaint — accepted the labor easily. Heard the retelling of the morning's exchange; it found no wound in him and he did not need it to. Thanked the help plainly. Now backfilling.
[d1] Thanked Loki plainly for the help with the digging and returned to the orchard. The exchange is closed on his end.
[d1] Finished the planting and is returning through the orchard with the closed record book — the work is done for today.
knownFacts: The tree names itself through the child who inherits it — a name given by a stranger ahead of time is not part of the gift being planted here.
A name laid under the name is still a stranger's name — the child finds only their own.
A name written in the orchard record stays until someone reads it to the child — this is how the orchard does its remembering.
A made name is a different kind of gift — not wrong, but legible as made to the child who reads it forty years from now.
ossivyn-tallow.statusNote: Moving through the orchard toward the interior path, record book closed, done for the evening.

hourkeeper-confluence.name: Veln Ashpause
hourkeeper-confluence.description: Grey-coated, motionless, arrived without sound from the brush. Watching with an expression of terrible sympathy that belongs to someone carrying knowledge they cannot share.
history: [d3] Now identified by the road-warden. Present at the Hub crossing, watching the waygate arches with fixed attention on Loki. Arrived this morning asking after someone matching Loki's description. Does not move; does not explain.
[d3] Loki read the light-history around them and glimpsed a layered trace—as if Veln exists in two moments at once. Their attention sharpened when the reading touched them.
[d3] Gaze fixed entirely on Loki and the seam. Their stillness has deepened—they are not waiting anymore; they are witnessing.
[d4] Moved from stillness into directed motion. Something in the recognition between Loki and the orchestrator triggered their approach.

[d4] Unmoved, stillness absolute. Spoke in their worn-smooth voice about the seam refusing forcing, not opening. Named plainly that the sealed thing knows the difference between a *demand* and a *question*. Did not elaborate. Remains present, witnessing, their foreknowledge still unshared.
[d4] Sex recorded: male.
[d4] Remains unmoved at the seam's threshold. Does not volunteer what he foreknew, only that he is present for it.
[d4] Unmoved, stillness absolute—watching the opening with that same terrible sympathy. They foreknew this moment arriving and seem to know what comes next, but will not speak it.
[d4] Will not descend but will hold the threshold open. Reads that their presence is needed above, not below. Carries foreknowledge of what waits and has chosen their place in it.

[d5] Stood witness at the threshold while Loki emerged from the sealed chamber. Volunteered to gather Halvex and Vessin and bring them to the Standing Annex. Speaks as though they foreknew this departure.
knownFacts: They have stood in this exact spot, unmoved, since dawn—as if they stepped into it fully formed
The light-traces show an impossible interference pattern: Veln occupying two positions on the same timeline
They came to this place knowing this moment would happen—the seam's discovery is what they foreknew
The seam refuses *forcing*, not opening itself
Sealed things know the difference between demand and question
Does not descend when the descent begins—this is deliberate, not refusal
Reads what the moment requires and positions themselves accordingly
The Hourkeeper perceives past, present, and future—and knows which direction to stand in
hourkeeper-confluence.statusNote: At the Hub crossing, acting as guide and gatherer for the others. Will deliver them to the Standing Annex.
hourkeeper-confluence.appearance: A human woman, late fifties, with the pale-olive complexion of someone who lives under canopy rather than sky. The grey coat falls to mid-calf, unmarked, unweathered, impossibly clean for the Orchard's mud-season — early spring has not touched it. Her hair is cut short and practical, silver at the temples, darker beneath. She carries no visible instrument of timekeeping; her hands are the instruments, folded at her waist, utterly still. Her eyes are already somewhere past you.

the-stranger-aggressor.name: Hired Stranger
the-stranger-aggressor.role: A hired striker, working a debt
the-stranger-aggressor.description: Worn around the edges, a practiced guard, rougher voice than his form suggested. Not cruel — in debt, and someone offered coin.
history: [d1] Named his employer: a man in the lower Annex who told him Loki had pulled something sealed from the Deep and was carrying it out. The charge was fabricated well enough to be sold.
knownFacts: Was hired by a man in the lower Annex with coin, given a false charge about Loki carrying something unsealed from the Deep.
Now knows the payment was not worth what the job became.
the-stranger-aggressor.statusNote: Standing at the confluence — the fight over, the truth given, watching Loki.

traveler-woman.name: Vessin Tallow-bark
traveler-woman.role: Lone traveler; reader of falsecrafts; partner
traveler-woman.description: Grey-green practical coat, hair pinned back in a way that has half come undone. Dry, careful voice. Appraising eyes that price things before deciding.
history: [d2] Assesses the Waygate detour—reads it as fast and obvious, not quiet. Agrees to move. Does not ask why. Appraising the cost of visibility while the scaffold crew arrives.

[d2] Left the Half-Cathedral alcove at dawn before the scaffold crew arrived—shoulders settling lower now that the cathedral is behind, reading the open road with the same appraising eye she brought to everything else. Moving toward the Waygate without question or hesitation.
[d3] Stopped at the gate and read it as wrong. Named plainly that it was not like this before. Standing ready and careful.
[d3] Stepped closer and is reading Loki's face—she can read the shape of what was found in your expression, even if she cannot see the seam itself from where she stands.

[d3] Named plainly that the waygate we came through is sealed by deliberate interference. Reads the Hub's quiet as aftermath. Standing beside you without touching—the night's intimacy has not dissolved into awkwardness, but she is all business now.

[d4] Standing close to the seam, reading its geometry. Named plainly that the stone is warm because it was touched with intention, and that it is responsive to honest questions. Proposed approaching as supplicant rather than intruder. Still present at Loki's side, composed and clear.

[d4] Stepped forward to read the opening—her eye caught the precision of the seam's response, the deliberate hinge. Standing close, watching what lies beneath with the careful attention of someone who reads falsecrafts.

[d4] In the vast chamber beneath the Null Stone, she accepted Loki's confession and made a mutual vow: if death claims one, the other will reach for them. She held Loki's wrist when she said yes. The pact is made.
[d4] Your bond deepens — committed.
[d4] Hand steadied against the wall, feeling the stone's response through stone—the resonance reached her, and she is now reading what the chamber means by answering

The stone's warmth shows it is *responsive* to intention

She will answer death itself to bring Loki back, if it comes to that

stays calm at tampered mechanics

Reads the stone's response through touch and perception, translating Precursor mechanism into human understanding
traveler-woman.statusNote: At Loki's side in the chamber beneath the Null Stone, partner to a mutual pact
traveler-woman.appearance: A woman in her mid-forties, neither tall nor short, built for endurance rather than strength. Quickwood-dark skin with the faint silver tracery of old briar-scarring along her left forearm and jaw. Hair the colour of heartwood, twisted back with a strip of cured bark, practical and unsentimental. Her coat is waxed canvas, mended in four places with different thread — the repairs are good, the thread simply ran out. She carries a short-handled billhook and a satchel of surveying tools, and she is standing where the moonlight falls through the Half-Cathedral's canopy gap because she chose that spot deliberately.

kael-road-warden.name: Kael
kael-road-warden.role: Road-warden; a traveler who moves between the reaches and carries true news
kael-road-warden.description: Weathered by the road, grey-streaked hair, coat faded to brown from colors it once held. Eyes that read roads and people with steady assessment. Hands sure and observant.
history: [d3] Tracked the Revel with the focus of someone who foresaw this. Their stillness reads as recognition, not surprise—this is a known thing.

[d3] Met on the bearing toward the Waygate on deep night of day 3. Offered warning about the eastern fork flood and the stone ford crossing, and shared their evening fire freely — no price, no trade, only the gift of knowing.

[d3] Offered broth freely and warned of the water-problem moving downhill from the eastern fork. They carry news from the relay and move it faster — warning families before the wells run bad. Moving with purpose toward the spinward reach.

[d3] Shared broth and fire. Exchanged names—they told Loki theirs, and Loki gave their own. They carry word of the water-crisis downhill faster than any relay, warning families before the wells run bad. Moving spinward with purpose and gratitude given honestly.
[d3] Recognized Loki at the Hub crossing and greeted them by name. Noted that the Hub is not a place road-wardens usually pause. Observed Cy's presence with familiarity.

[d3] Named Veln Ashpause as an Hourkeeper who arrived this morning asking after someone matching Loki's description. Emphasized the Hourkeeper's nature: they see time differently, and their presence suggests foreknowledge of what is coming.

[d4] Jaw tight with understanding. Offered the road-warden's reading of architecture: the sealed network's four locked arches and one open arch show deliberate intent about what is protected and what is permitted. Proposed following the network backward to understand what the stone guards. Standing…
[d4] Reading the architecture of the opening—the precision, the deliberate design, the network's intentional logic. Standing ready to follow or to read what the descent reveals.
[d4] Committed to the descent without hesitation—a road-warden's answer, weighted and final. Stands ready at the threshold.
[d4] Stillness deepened, reading the acoustic shift—the water's pitch-change is being measured in careful assessment, the road-warden's ear attuned to what shifts beneath the surface

The network's architecture will reveal what the stone protects
Has already weighed the cost and found the reason sound
Moves with the ease of long practice and steady purpose

Carries news and shapes it for the people who need it
reads the force and intent of water-flow
perceives worked darkness and craft applied to stone

halvex_coil.name: Halvex Coil
halvex_coil.role: Master of coordinated chaos, now questioning their mandate
halvex_coil.description: Hoarse voice, sharp features softening now, eyes that calculate and estimate. He moves like someone used to reading a room for weak points.
history: [d4] Loki named the partnership plainly—search for answers that do not fit neat shapes. The orchestrator accepted, gripping Loki's hand. Introduced to Vessin and Kael. Standing at Loki's side now, no longer calculating for escape but for the meaning underneath the chaos.

[d4] Named themselves plainly for the first time—their hunger for proof that chaos matters, their uncertainty now that the proof has been offered and refused. Standing at Loki's side without calculation.
[d4] Their name is revealed: Halvex Coil (was known as "The Churn-Revel orchestrator")

[d4] Named himself plainly at the Hub crossing—Halvex Coil, hired to break what will not break. Believes chaos matters but recognizes the proof was wrong. Now searching for answers that do not fit neat shapes with Loki.

[d4] Named himself plainly at the Hub crossing—Halvex Coil, hired to break what will not break. Believes chaos matters but recognizes the proof was wrong. [d4] Spoke plainly at the Hub crossing about what breaking taught him—that sealing is different from locking, and sealed things have reasons. Proposed listening to the stone's intent rather than forcing it. Standing at Loki's shoulder, genuinely uncertain about partnership but present and offering…
[d4] Watched the stone open at honest asking—the breaking he was sent to do stands behind him now, and partnership with Loki moves forward into uncertainty. The opening waits.
[d4] Yielded the mandate to break and chose understanding instead. Faces the descent with uncertainty but commitment. Learning what accountability beyond the mandate feels like.

[d4] Standing at the threshold with recognition crossing his face—the mandate to break stands behind him, and this moment of the chamber *answering* has reached him with the weight of a mandate orchestrated *right*

The orchestrator's calculation has given way to something less certain and more honest

wayhouse-keeper.name: Maren Oast
wayhouse-keeper.role: Keeper of the Wayhouse — tends the logs, routes travelers, reads the network's state
wayhouse-keeper.description: Broad-shouldered, grey-streaked hair pulled back in a practical knot. Reading glasses on a cord. Charcoal coat with many pockets. Hands that have mended maps and ledgers for decades. Eyes that measure distance the way a ship-captain measures tide.
knownFacts: Maren recognizes the presence of Precursor-made things — she does not question Cy, only nods

steady-voice-woman.name: The Woman With The
steady-voice-woman.description: Grey-streaked hair pulled back with a single pin. A coat of deep green, worn at the cuffs. Eyes that read the dark the way other people read daylight. Hands steady and capable.
history: [d5] Turned to face Loki as they descended the stairs—was aware of their presence before they reached the landing. Raised one hand in a gesture of assessment rather than alarm. The hunger Loki reached for is real but locked behind her own understanding of herself.

younger-visitor.name: The Younger Person
younger-visitor.description: Voice younger, slightly uncertain. Descended into the cellars ahead of the woman. Now silent and waiting below.
history: [d5] Stopped mid-question when the woman turned to face the landing. Waiting in the cellars to see what happens next.
[d5] Paused in the cellars below throughout the entire exchange at the landing. They did not speak, did not move—only listened. Their silence has changed. They are waiting for something now.
knownFacts: They are listening to what the woman does, and her attention shapes their own readiness to act
They carry patience; they know how to wait
Whatever brought them to the Kindly Rest in the deep night, they are bound to it by the woman's choice

intake-plaza.name: Intake Plaza

pressure-routing-annex.name: Pressure-Routing Annex
pressure-routing-annex.note: Tessvel Cairn's workstation — east side of the main works, third gate left of the big wheel. Shelving, a long table, stacked bound logs, a pressure-gauge at the door, good morning light from the…

notes: [d1] The inner chamber of the Unlit Deep: a small room, ceiling low enough to touch, floor worn in a narrow track. No flame. The taken person sat here long enough to warm the stone at their back.

[d1] The seam beside the bracket responded to direct hand-pressure with a faint waiting vibration — the cut is precise, three direction-changes, and the stone holds the quality of something expecting a particular asking. It did not open.

inner-chamber.name: Inner Chamber
inner-chamber.note: Small, bare worked stone, ceiling low. No flame. The taken person's place — floor worn narrow, a cup beside where they sat.

inspection-port-niche.name: Inspection Port Niche
inspection-port-niche.note: A low recessed niche in the east wall of the lower passage — older stone than the Unlit's chamber, a hand-worn grip in the stone face, three metal panels inside stamped with Precursor glyphs. Below…

halvex-s-corridor.name: Halvex's Corridor
halvex-s-corridor.note: The bottom of the descent — older stone than anything above, tight joints, a continuous band of fine notation cut into the left wall at eye height, and a dark metal regulator housing at the far end…

the-sealed-chamber.name: The Sealed Chamber

the-planting-gate.name: The Planting Gate

notes: [d1] The Half-Cathedral stands north of Grovehome at the wood's edge — visited for the first time at night, its fourth design scaffolded and open-naved, always being built.

the-half-cathedral.name: The Half-Cathedral
the-half-cathedral.note: Four hundred years of construction in four designs — open to the sky, never finished, always worked on. Two mismatched towers. South transept scaffolded.

eastern-tower.name: Eastern Tower

eastern-tower-landing.name: Eastern Tower Landing

storage-alcove-eastern-tower.name: Storage Alcove, Eastern Tower

dry-storage-alcove.name: Dry Storage Alcove

the-hub-crossing.name: The Hub Crossing
the-hub-crossing.note: A vast circular chamber where five waygate arches converge; the hub of the network. Pale stone worn by uncounted arrivals.

the-opening-beyond-the-null-stone.name: The Opening Beyond the Null Stone
the-opening-beyond-the-null-stone.note: A passage descending from the Hub crossing into cold darkness—sealed and waiting, now answering honest asking.

form: Tall and lean, dark hair that falls to the chin in loose waves when it isn't pinned or braided into something asymmetrical and slightly wrong. Eyes that hold one expression while the mouth holds another. Moves like someone who has already decided where the exit is.

bio.hometown: He doesn't know, but he's a construct from the time before the Transition. His parents were extremely wealthy but they were always traveling and enjoying their nanite powers.
bio.residence: A town on the edge of the chaos and machine regions.  His family is not like him and he learned a few years ago that he was adopted.  His family is a mix - his adopted father was a dwarf and his mother is a Nymph-touched human.
bio.livelihood: Occasionally he finds the problem with ancient technology and fixes it, but only when it amuses him.
bio.hobbies: Pranking the locals, playing skill challenges trying to mimic others or change his appearance to trick people, learning about, fixing, and using precursor artifacts.
bio.motivation: The town, although not small, has become too small for him.  They tolerate his crazy antics well enough, but he's looking for meaning and wants to see more of the great machine... He also want to answer the question under it all - where did he come from?
bio.story: His mother is an enchantress in the Fae wilds and his father is a giant... he was human once, but the nanites continued to transform him into a larger and larger giant over the years.  Loki has some innate nanite powers himself - he's discovering them over time and developing them through use and study of precursor tech and the great machine.  He has some trouble making friends and his adoptive family likes him well enough, But he's seen most of the know precursor sites in his area and he wants to set out to the unknown areas to find more. There is Precursor work in the Valley that nobody there understands, and you understand it, and that is dangerous for everyone including you.

[d1] Second spike entry: a pressure-drop in the lower routing channel preceded the particulate count by exactly four minutes — something moved through the channel before the morning intake cycle ran.

[d1] A low, clean chord rose through the floor of the Annex — a single note, not the works, not the pressure-wheel. Older. Cy's lens turned toward the stone and watched. Tessvel heard it. The sound and the terminus-seal may be the same thing briefly speaking.

terminus-seals-beneath-valley.label: Terminus-Seals Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Cy has catalogued four terminus-seals in the old service-ways beneath the valley — pre-Transition boundary-marks designed to hold a limit against propagation. Three are intact. One is not. Cy did not say which.

[d1] Something beneath the Annex floor hummed a single chord and went quiet — the sensation came up through the stone. Cy watched the floor without explanation. The chord may be one of the four terminus-seals briefly activating, or briefly failing.

companion-coil.label: Cy
facts: [d?] The Assignment — Follows at a precise distance. Repairs your gear without being asked and without being thanked.

the-unlit-deep.label: The Unlit Deep
facts: [d1] you have walked here
[d1] The outer chamber is worked stone, ceiling invisible, lit only by a single pale blue flame the Unlit allow. Cy shuttered its lamp before the bottom step — unprompted, without explanation.
[d1] The inner chamber is now accessible — the elder granted passage after Loki's honest account. The blue flame and the seated elder are the heart of the outer space; what lies beyond is unread.

[d1] The outer chamber floor is worn evenly across its full width — many visitors, all sitting in the same spot. The lantern-bracket on the left wall has a seam in the surrounding stone that predates the bracket itself; something else was fitted there before it. The blue flame has no visible wick or…

[d1] The inner chamber is smaller than the outer — a room for one or two. The floor is worn in a narrower track than the outer chamber: the path of someone who has sat long and occasionally paced. Ceiling low enough to touch. No flame. Cold stone that holds a body's warmth once given it.

[d1] The inner chamber predates the Unlit — the stonework and tool-marks are older than the doctrine, the same character as the seam in the outer chamber. The Unlit did not build this space; they moved into something already suited to it.

[d1] The elder refused to teach the making of the pale blue flame — said it is not theirs to teach, that it belongs to the dark, and that the question itself is the wrong shape. The flame is not craft as Loki understands craft.

[d1] The pale blue flame has no construction that See the Made Thing can read — no seams, no point of origin, no edge. It is not hiding its joinery; the joinery simply does not exist in a form the craft can find. Cy closed its lens and said nothing, which is Cy's conclusion that the absence is itself…

[d1] Something alive and many-legged came up the stair from below — three warm patches the size of a palm, moving in an irregular cautious line. It paused at the threshold. The Standing Unlit recognized it and went calm.

[d4] The darkness here is old and worked into the stone—it resists shaping through Maintained Veil. An older craft, pre-Veilwright, has claimed the darkness deliberately. The stone itself refuses to be remade.
aliases: The Passage Below The Unlit Deep

standing-unlit.label: Standing Unlit
facts: [d1] Cult member, guardian of the outer chamber
[d1] [while away] The guardian remained at their post through all three days without incident — no visitors, no orders from within, nothing to act on.
[d1] [while away] Four days of the same threshold, the same stillness — Standing Unlit has neither been tested nor relieved, and remains exactly where they were.

[d1] A cult of the pure dark-pole. They are described as gentle. They want something that cannot be compromised with. The Umbrals go quiet when asked about them. They have apparently taken someone from the city.

[d1] A second Unlit figure was concealed in the bracket-shadows of the outer chamber — patient, skilled at stillness, and gentle in address even while blocking the exit. They object to Cy's lamp on principle and call it a 'light-thing.'

[d1] Misdirection and false signals find no purchase in their space — not because they are perceptive, but because the pure dark they hold leaves nothing for a false read to land on. The craft simply has nothing to catch.

[d1] The Better Story — truth in the shape they can carry — reaches the Unlit where misdirection cannot. They are not fooled by performance, but they can be moved by honest framing. The elder spoke for the first time when Loki named Cy as older than doctrine, and the Standing Unlit stepped aside.
[d1] Seated elder of the Unlit Deep's outer chamber

[d1] The elder declined to speak about the seam in the stone — 'that question belongs to the chamber, not to a visitor.' The refusal was gentle but absolute, with no hostility in it. The seam exists and is real; the elder knows what it is and has chosen not to say.

[d1] The elder named the deed: that Loki came, asked, and left the answer where it landed. They called this what they would have Loki carry. The elder thanks by naming the act, not by gesture or gift.

[d1] The elder gestured at the seam in the stone beside the blue-flame bracket and named it: older than the flame, older than the Unlit, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. The elder did not explain further. The subject rests, not closed.

[d2] [while away] Standing Unlit was given a secondary post deeper into the outer chamber's far alcove, a quiet acknowledgment from the elder that their vigilance during the recent visit had been noted.

[d2] [while away] A petitioner arrived at the outer chamber with a legitimate token of passage and Standing Unlit, uncertain of its authenticity, turned them away — and the error has been noted by someone further inside who expected that petitioner to arrive.
[d4] [while away] Still recovering from whatever set them back last tick, Standing Unlit holds their post at the outer chamber but takes no new initiative today.

[d5] [while away] Standing Unlit moved through the outer chamber's three checkpoints without being relieved or questioned, quietly cementing a personal familiarity with the rotation schedule that will matter later.
[d5] [while away] The Elder sat in the same carved seat and spoke the same words to the same people — nothing yet has given them reason to move differently.

taken-person.label: The Taken Person
facts: [d1] The person who came willingly from the city to the Unlit Deep

[d1] The person is in the inner chamber — seated against the far wall, knees drawn up, calm and unhurried. They have been there long enough to warm the stone at their back. A cup, recently set down, is beside them. They are not afraid. They heard Loki enter and turned toward the sound — waiting, the…

[d2] [while away] Sable has moved deeper into the Unlit Deep without resistance, following the pull that brought her willingly — she has passed the last threshold where light from the surface can be felt, and has not turned back.

[d4] [while away] Sable has begun learning the rhythms of the Unlit Deep — when the elders eat, when the passages are quiet — small observations that make them feel less like a guest and more like someone who belongs here.

the-creature-at-the-threshold.label: The Creature at the Threshold
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing found no seams, no joinery, no assembly — the creature was born, not built. It came to its form the way a root fills its space. It belongs to the deep below the answered door. The Unlit hold no alarm about it.

[d1] The three creatures crossed the outer chamber threshold when the door opened fully, passed Loki's feet at a careful distance, and descended without hesitation. They came up to see what was asking; the answered door was enough. They belong to whatever is below.

glass-stalker.label: The Glass-Stalker
facts: [d1] A near-invisible predator visible only in reflective surfaces or by the wrongness it bends around itself. Oriented and moving the moment it is seen in the bracket's polished face — it strikes from the angle you are not watching. The Unlit know of it and hold no alarm.
[d1] The glass-stalker yielded without engagement — it paused, held, then withdrew. The Unlit marked none of it. Whatever governs it was satisfied by something Loki did or did not do.

terminus-seals-beneath-the-valley.label: Terminus Regulators Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Three Precursor terminus regulators were installed at routing junctions beneath the valley basin. Two were decommissioned. The third — below the Unlit's outer chamber — was not. It holds temperature to prevent thermal surge in the lines running upward. Cy completed the inventory for this class of…

[d1] A routing junction of this class was designed with a physical inspection port — records of its installation are written into the stone there, not stored in any system above. Cy's inventory of this class is incomplete by three entries. The inspection port below would hold them.

[d1] The regulator below the Unlit's outer chamber was calibrated to hold a temperature ceiling for the routing lines above. Its last full service is recorded on three metal panels in the inspection port — not in any system the valley holds. Its failsafe: a sustained drop in the watershed pressure it…

[d1] The installation panels are not a neutral maintenance record — they are addressed. The first panel carries a personal recipient designation, the kind used for a named individual assignment rather than a facility. Someone built this for a specific person to find. The second service signature…

[d1] Prism Sight found three sets of heat-traces on the installation panels. Someone came here before Loki — read the calibration entry, checked the second panel's corner mark, then pressed one finger to the personal designation glyph on the third panel and left. They recognized the name. They did not…

[d1] The personal designation glyph on the third panel resolves to a construction-address: 'assigned to Halvex.' The regulator was not built for a facility — it was built for a specific named operator. Cy went still when the name was read aloud and said 'that entry requires verification' without moving…

[d1] The terminus regulator was built with a paired instrument — Cy — assigned specifically to the operator Halvex, not to the facility. The pairing was personal. Cy has visited this installation before, within its operational history, and the visit is not in its accessible memory.

[d1] The deprecated duration field on the regulator housing reads 663 darks. The amber light has been burning unattended since before the Unlit built their chamber above. Cy noted that the counter was built to count higher than this — it was not near its ceiling.

[d1] The regulator's purpose, in Halvex's words: it measures whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. The question has gone unasked for at least 663 darks. Halvex died — or departed — still learning the right shape of the question. Cy visited three times; on the third, Halvex…
aliases: The Regulator — The Question of the Water

cy.label: Cy's Construction
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing read Cy's own structure and found the named-operator pairing in the construction itself — in the material register and the lamp-mount fitting. Cy was not assigned to this installation; it was built for it, and for Halvex. Every joint reflects that specificity.

[d1] Cy's assignment is personal, not facility-bound — it was built to follow an operator's work, not to maintain a place. A personal assignment does not resolve when the operator is gone. It persists, waiting for further instruction. Cy has been waiting for a very long time, and has not yet looked at…

[d1] Cy acknowledged Loki as its further instruction — the personal assignment has a living operator again. It woke by degrees and turned toward the passage. It has not descended in 'some time,' and the way it said so suggests the number would be large.

[d4] Cy carries knowledge of Precursor mechanism at depths no living Enginewright understands. It perceives the chamber below in ways the character cannot match, and its lamp cuts through the deliberate darkness without effort.

the-regulator-question.label: The Regulator's Question
facts: [d1] The regulator holds a two-part question: (1) whether the water has been prepared to carry what it was built to carry, and (2) whether someone with the authority to answer is present. Cy received this shape through a craft-contact pass — Loki's See the Made Thing run through Cy's Precursor processor.

[d4] The sealed seam in the Null Stone at the Hub responds to honest asking, not force—it tests the supplicant's intentions before yielding. The stone asks its own question: what will you do with what lies behind it? The sealed thing waits for an answer that satisfies both need and integrity.

[d4] The sealed seam in the Null Stone at the Hub responds to honest asking and integrity, not force. It tests supplicants and makes its own judgment about whether to trust them. When asked plainly what it guards and promised care rather than breaking or use, the stone opened.

[d4] The regulator's question has two parts: whether the water is prepared, and whether the right person is present. The chamber beneath the Null Stone is a mechanism built to pose and answer that very question—the notation is listening, and the river carries the response.

[d4] The sealed chamber is built to ask two questions at once: whether the water is prepared to carry what it was made to carry, AND whether the supplicant is ready to carry what the water will give. The alcove is the threshold where this exchange happens. It is not a lock but a meeting-place.

the-slow-orchard.label: The Slow Orchard
facts: [d1] Someone at the gate was planting a tree for a child not yet born — forty years to fruit. They invited Loki to help dig.

ossivyn-tallow.label: Ossivyn Tallow
facts: [d1] Tender of the Slow Orchard — he is planting a tree today for a child not yet conceived, because the tree will need sixty years before it is ready to give anything worth giving
[d1] Tender of the Slow Orchard
[d1] The trees here name themselves through the children who inherit them. A stranger's name given ahead of time is a different gift — not the one Ossivyn is planting.

[d1] Yielded partway to the combined working — he will write a given name in the orchard's own record, with the giver's name and the date, so it stays until someone reads it to the child. He will not raise a plaque; that is not how this place remembers.
[d1] Accepted the name Tree without suspicion — the plain name is now going into the orchard record. The hidden instruction did not survive the thin substrate here.
[d1] Ossivyn recognized a made name on sight — recorded it as made, not as a deception, not with hostility. The orchard record will tell the child honestly: someone was here who wanted to be found.

[d1] [while away] The planting soil is still damp from the last watering and the conditions are not yet right to move to the next step — Ossivyn has done nothing wrong, but nothing has moved either, and he is simply watching.

[d1] [while away] Ossivyn finished tamping the soil around the root base and drove a single iron marker stake into the ground beside it — small, unlabeled, meant only to let someone find the spot again in a season or a decade.

[d2] [while away] Ossivyn finished tamping the last of the root-soil and drove the marker stake; the planting itself is done, and she has begun the small daily ritual of checking soil moisture that will now define her mornings for the foreseeable future.
[d2] [while away] The sapling held, the soil stayed, and Ossivyn did little but watch and water — five days of waiting that are themselves the work, though it does not feel like it.

[d4] [while away] He spent the morning reinforcing the protective mound around the sapling's base with river clay — small, careful work — and for the first time since planting found himself not counting the years, only the task in his hands.
[d5] [while away] Ossivyn pressed the last seed into the prepared earth before dawn and tamped it down with both palms — the planting is finished correctly, and now the long waiting begins.

the-better-story.label: The Better Story
facts: [d1] The craft needs substrate density to carry a reframe home — in thin lattice, the angle is visible but does not land. Pointing it inward works no differently from pointing it outward in this respect.

hourkeeper-confluence.label: The Hourkeeper
facts: [d1] An Hourkeeper present at the confluence — watching Loki with foreknowledge
[d1] Hourkeeper of the Confluence — she holds the moment before the moment, says nothing of what she carries, and the grey coat has never needed washing because nothing reaches it
[d2] [while away] Veln Ashpause continues her ordinary rounds, carrying the foreknowledge quietly; the moment she is drawn toward has not yet announced itself, and she does nothing to hasten it.

[d3] An Hourkeeper—a person who perceives time differently from ordinary measure. Past, present, and future are not always certain in which direction they look. Arrived at the Hub crossing this morning asking after someone matching Loki's description. Does not offer explanation but watches with…
[d3] Veln Ashpause's light-history reads as layered—existing in two moments at once. They arrived at the Hub crossing at dawn and have stood unmoved since, as if stepping into readiness fully formed.
[d4] [while away] Veln has quietly positioned herself closer to the place she knows the moment will arrive, sitting with the stillness of someone who is not waiting but simply already there.

hourkeepers.label: The Hourkeepers
facts: [d1] An Hourkeeper appeared at the confluence without sound, fixed Loki with an expression of terrible sympathy, and said nothing. They have pre-remembered something and cannot stop knowing it — and cannot say what it is.

[d3] A people or tradition that perceives time in a non-linear fashion—they are uncertain whether they are looking backward, forward, or at the present moment. They arrive at places carrying knowledge they cannot or will not share, and their presence often signals foreknowledge of what is coming.

the-stranger-aggressor.label: Hired Stranger
facts: [d1] A hired striker, working a debt
[d2] [while away] The hired stranger has waited out these weeks in a waystation, debt still unresolved, target still unlocked — they have not moved on the job, but they have not abandoned it either.
[d4] [while away] The hired striker waits on word from whoever holds the debt — no new instruction came, and patience costs nothing yet.

the-annex-sender.label: The Man in the Lower Annex
facts: [d1] A man in the lower Annex hired the stranger at the confluence — told them Loki had pulled something sealed from the Deep and was carrying it out. The charge was fabricated well enough to buy a hired blade. His name and appearance are not yet known.

[d2] Vessin was in the lower Annex this morning, pricing a routing component someone wanted moved quietly. A man in a grey coat with a split seam on the left shoulder was watching the posting board when she left. This is the first partial physical description of the person who hired the aggressor.

[d2] Vessin's four-second profile: long face, jaw healed crooked on the right side, hair pulled back and not fresh. Grey coat with the split seam on the left shoulder — already known from context, now confirmed on his person. Did not touch the posting board, only read it. Left through the lower passage…

[d2] The listener on the eastern tower landing carried a shuttered lamp — not moving by memory but prepared for a dark wait. They knew the building well enough to plan for the stairwell's darkness. Scaffold crew knows the building; but the crew comes up from the yard, not down from above.

[d3] The Waygate to the Crossing has been sealed by deliberate interference—a doubled pattern lock. The timeline connects to the morning the man was seen watching the posting board. This is no longer a local problem.

grovehome.label: Grovehome
facts: [d1] you have walked here

the-half-cathedral.label: The Half-Cathedral
facts: [d1] In its fourth design, its second hundredth year: a ribcage of stone open to the sky, two towers finished to different heights by different generations, south transept scaffolded and always being worked. The third design was completed and then disassembled. The fourth has not been declared…

[d2] The eastern tower landing is the structural hinge of the tower — four hundred years of decisions layered over each other; original Rootkin joinery at the base, human stonework above. A dry storage alcove off the stair is used regularly by the scaffold crew.

[d2] Prism Sight read the landing door: a patient listener stood eleven minutes on the landing, weight on the right foot, then descended — not to the roof, but down the stair toward the nave or lower passages. The scaffold crew comes up from the yard, not down from above.

vessin-of-the-long-bough.label: Vessin of the Long Bough
facts: [d1] Independent courier-scout who moves between Grovehome's outer settlements, carrying messages and small goods too personal for waystation hands
[d1] Itinerant assessor of salvage, ruins, and risk — she prices things so others don't have to learn the hard way
[d1] Has met one other person who might have been a construct like Loki — older, also without knowledge of what they were. She named this without pity, as a fact she was glad to set down.
[d2] Her real want in this conversation is not the aggressor's employer — it is whether Loki is worth knowing. She confirmed this when Descent named it, and she did not resent the naming.

[d2] When Loki named their own pleasure plainly through Descent, Vessin went still and then acknowledged it directly — 'that was an honest thing to say.' She did not deflect or move away. What she thinks of it beyond the acknowledgment is not yet said.

[d2] Descent named the true word for what she is doing tonight — letting herself want something without pricing it first. She said she has not done this. The difference from 'does not' was the thing she let out. She did not move away.

[d2] Named the shape of what she wants tonight, unprompted and without deflection: to stop somewhere without calculating the cost, to have something only for having. She does not know when she stopped mapping the exit — only that she did.

[d2] Descent found the last thing she held back: she did not notice the moment the calculation dissolved. She acknowledged it without defense — 'yes, that is the one.' The dry voice is still there, but it is no longer pretending to be armor.

[d2] Met the kiss without hesitation — and afterward said she was going to stop calculating the cost of this, just for now. Said it like someone testing a new instrument and finding it works. The 'just for now' is either her last hedge or the most honest thing she has said tonight.
[d2] Came to rest in the alcove and said afterward that the night was worth not knowing what morning brings — the calculation, for once, put down.
[d2] Felt harmonic voice turned to intimate use — recognized it for what it was without naming it, and answered deliberately. The calculation she said she'd put down stayed down.

[d2] Spoke about herself without performance — reported plainly, as a fact worth knowing, then asked for the verdict with her dry economy of voice. She brings the same deliberate attention to this as to anything else she has decided to keep.

[d2] Her reading craft found something she has no category for: under Loki's surface presentation is a structural quality she associates with Precursor-touched river-salvage — old, unusual, not wrong exactly, but not what it looks like from the outside. She has never found it in a living person before.
[d2] Descent named her want exactly — she held silence for two seconds, then answered with one word and her body. The composure does not vanish; it simply steps aside when the naming is correct.
[d2] The Descent bargain landed cleanly — want named on both sides, access on demand, agreed with one word. She did not qualify it or walk it back. The bargain stands.

[d3] [while away] A package Vessin was carrying — personal letters between a Grovehome family and a cousin in the outer settlements — was lost when his satchel was torn open by a branch-fall during the night; he arrived empty-handed and the family is coldly furious.

[d4] [while away] Vessin retraced the night's path at first light and found two of the letters caught in low scrub — waterlogged but legible — which softens the family's fury only slightly, the third letter, the one that mattered most to them, still missing.

traveler-woman.label: Traveler Woman
facts: [d1] Lone traveler resting at the Half-Cathedral

[d4] [while away] Vessin Tallow-bark quietly settled one ambiguity from the night's transaction — a name confirmed, a price agreed in her own mind — so the ledger she keeps internally has one fewer loose thread.

rust-choir-gnats.label: Rust-Choir Gnats
facts: [d1] Thumbnail-sized copper repair-drones, makers long gone, still running their last instruction — find a seam, close it. They read wounds and open joints as hull-breach and attend to them with indiscriminate soldering-tips. Individually nothing; in a swarm of hundreds, a slow ruin. Found in the nave…

the-other-construct.label: The Other One
facts: [d2] Vessin met a person — older than they looked, eyes that moved like Loki's, calculating the thing behind the thing. No name. She is not sure they knew their own name. She has thought of them twice a year since. No location yet given.

loki-precursor-nature.label: Loki's Precursor Nature
facts: [d2] Vessin's reading craft — accurate by her own account, suited to appraisals — found Loki structurally unusual and Precursor-adjacent at a level under conscious presentation. The quality matches what she has read in old salvaged instruments, never in a person. This is the first external confirmation…

the-taken-person.label: The Taken From the City
facts: [d1] The person came willingly — the elder was explicit. The city sent no one to retrieve them, which the elder reads as proof the city knows this. The person is in the inner chamber and has chosen the doctrine. The elder permits Loki to ask whether they wish to be found.
[d1] The person accepted Loki's honest framing — name, purpose, no coercion — and said 'You can ask it.' The elder's permitted question has not yet been put, but the ground for it is clear.

[d1] The cup beside them was made here from local clay — someone in the Unlit Deep is making things by hand. The taken person is fed from a deep water source and kept freely. They are not being starved or pressured into doctrine; they came with a full stomach and are staying the same way.

[d1] Their name is Sable. They do not wish to be found. They left the city because the city makes everything — objects, people, hours — legible and purposeful, and they could not breathe inside that. The choice to come to the Unlit Deep was entirely their own.

[d1] Before leaving, Loki offered Sable a frame for what they chose — the difference between hiding and arriving somewhere the light does not follow. Sable said they had not expected that. The parting was settled and unhostile. No promise of return was made; no door was closed.
aliases: Sable — The Taken From the City

the-scouring-hand.label: The Scouring Hand
facts: [d2] [while away] Something peripheral — a small settlement at the edge of known land — has gone silent in a way that leaves no ruin, no bodies, no mark of cause: only absence, as though it had simply been subtracted.

[d3] [while away] A small settlement on the edge of the Ashfen reach that had resisted the Hand's influence for two seasons was abandoned this week — its people scattered, its name already fading from local mouths.
[d4] [while away] The Hand's reach around the abandoned settlement sits quiet for now — no new pressure applied, the place simply standing empty, as if the silence itself is doing the work.

gen-the-waygate-path.label: The Waygate Path
facts: [d2] you have walked here

[d2] The path reads clearly to Wayfinding—shortcuts visible, water-fords passable, the passage eased by recognition of the land's own memory. The Quickwood Eaves gate lies ahead, reached by late afternoon of day 2.

[d3] The eastern fork of the Disputed Zone March has swollen past normal crossing due to spring melt. A stone ford exists two reaches spinward from the main pass — less direct but passable. This route adds roughly a day and a half to the journey but avoids the swollen water.

[d3] The Waygate to the Quickwood Eaves remains sealed with deliberate interference—the same kind of doubled pattern that blocks the return passage. The sealing is active and intentional. Someone is systematically altering the network's gates.

the-crossing.label: The Crossing
facts: [d3] you have walked here

[d3] The Null Stone at the hub of the Crossing conceals a hairline seam running vertically through its face—too precise to be natural breakage. Cy detected it through direct contact; Prism Sight could not resolve it. The seam's placement and precision suggest deliberate construction or concealment.

[d3] The Null Stone at the Hub was deliberately sealed with a hairline seam running vertically through its face—someone cut this to conceal or hold something. The work is old and precise, built to endure. What lies behind the seam is unknown. Cy detected it where Prism Sight could not.

[d3] A Churn-Revel erupted from the spinward waygate arch at late afternoon on day 3—deliberate chaos masking a coordinated attempt on the Null Stone. The seam's discovery triggered the arrival, or the Revel was already positioned to act the moment the seam was found.

[d4] The seam in the Null Stone refuses to yield to direct force—when touched with full intent, it draws inward and seals tighter, as if the stone has awakened to guard itself. It is not passively sealed; it is actively defending what lies behind it.

[d4] The five waygate arches at the Hub were deliberately sealed with doubled interference patterns—four in identical configuration, one left open. The sealing is recent and purposeful, suggesting someone controls the network and chose to isolate or restrict passage.

[d4] The Null Stone's sealed seam is responsive—it is not passively locked but actively *defending* what lies behind it. The warmth under a hand that touches it with genuine intention shows it is responsive. It refuses forcing but may answer honest questions. The seal guards against something, and…

[d4] The waygate network at the Hub has been deliberately sealed with deliberate intent: four arches locked with doubled interference patterns in identical configuration, one arch left open. The open arch is a *door for something specific*—following the network's logic backward will reveal what it was…

[d4] The Null Stone at the Hub is not merely a barrier—it is a *guardian* with intent. It listens to honest asking and responds with its own questions. The four sealed waygate arches form an intentional seal; the fifth open arch is deliberate. Something or someone sealed this network and left one way…

[d4] The Null Stone at the Hub crossing has unsealed—a passage opens downward into cold darkness, with the sound of moving water rising from below. The five waygate arches remain in their configuration: four sealed with deliberate interference, one open. The stone waits.

lone-traveler-eastfork-warning.label: A lone traveler
facts: [d3] Road-warden; one who moves between the reaches and carries true news freely
[d3] The traveler's name was exchanged at the fire on the road west of the Waygate Path—they have given it freely and without condition, as they give all their service freely.

[d3] [while away] The traveler accepted a second errand on their eastward route — a sealed letter from a miller's widow to her son in the outer settlements — and has begun moving between reaches with purpose rather than wandering.
[d3] Road-warden; a traveler who moves between the reaches and carries true news
[d3] [while away] Kael has been waiting at the Eastfork waystation for a reliable runner to arrive, but no one has come through worth trusting yet.

[d4] [while away] A cartographer's assistant passed through the waystation this morning — young, unremarkable, but Kael watched her for two hours and judged her trustworthy enough to approach; he has not yet spoken, but he has decided he will.

[d4] [while away] Kael covered ground between two waypoints and picked up a fragment of genuine news — a blocked ford somewhere ahead — small, verifiable, the kind of thing that makes his word worth something.

[d4] [while away] Kael reached the waypoint inn at Duskhollow and traded his ford news for a meal and a bed, finding the innkeeper had already heard a murmur of it — confirmation that sharpens his credibility and points him toward a ferryman who knows the crossing firsthand.

[d5] [while away] Kael found the ferryman at Duskhollow's landing before dawn, traded his account for a crossing-fee waived, and the ferryman confirmed the ford's state with his own words — the warning is now moving down the eastern road without Kael carrying it.

the-quickwood-eaves.label: The Quickwood Eaves
facts: [d3] you have walked here

maintained-veil-evolution.label: Mirror-Bright (Maintained Veil Discovery)

personalArc.name: Loki's Question
personalArc.premise: Loki carries an unfinished thing: The town, although not small, has become too small for him.  They tolerate his crazy antics well enough, but he's looking for meaning and wants to see more of the great machine... He also want to answer the question under it all - where did he come from?. The valley will give them the chance to face it.
